original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: For every source count n, decide whether the unsigned F3 connector (n immutable sources, all 2^n-1 nonzero binary-mask outputs, one arbitrarily dirty restored connector) attains the per-operator floor of three calls per operator, 3(n+2^n-1) calls.
scope_change_reason: Keeps the F3 alphabet of PR4189/PR4225 and increases the source count, which the card lists as a scope-change trigger. It decides whether the F3 alphabet's three-per-operator price survives for larger batches, the premise any larger-batch F3 consumer would rely on. The F2 analogue of PR943 loses its floor at five sources.
bottleneck_link: Bounds the batch size at which an F3 connector consumer can pay exactly three calls per operator. No physical consumer, admission or transfer is supplied, so no kappa change follows.
stop_rule: Stop after floor words for n<=6, the counting exclusion for n>=14, the deletion lemma and one explicit seven-source upper bound. Exact status of n=7..13 is left open; solver and local-search runs are reported as search failures only.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json supplies restored source paths for n=1..6 and a 21-event seven-source path. verify.py regenerates every readout triple, simulates the literal words with generic noncommuting coefficients, checks the deletion lemma on all 20 single-source deletions, the counting table for n<=64 and five rejection controls.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Is the three-per-operator floor attained for n=7, i.e. is the seven-source optimum 402 or 405 calls?
open_questions.why_it_matters: By the deletion lemma this single case decides whether the attaining set is exactly n<=6; otherwise the threshold lies between 7 and 13.
open_questions.first_step: Run an exhaustive or proof-producing search over restored 21-event paths up to source relabelling, using the window form of README section 3 and a checked UNSAT certificate.
open_questions.blocked_by: A plain SAT encoding did not finish within its time limit; no checkable unsatisfiability proof exists yet.

open_questions.question: What is the exact optimum for each n>=7 once the floor fails?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A consumer of a large F3 batch needs the exact surcharge, not only that it is positive.
open_questions.first_step: Lower-bound the number of masks realizable by three readouts on a path with S source events, then trade longer source paths against six-readout outputs.
open_questions.blocked_by: No lower bound beyond the next multiple of three is proved here.

open_questions.question: Does a concrete consumer use an n-source unsigned F3 batch with a favorable complete invoice?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The abstract call counts change no recursive supplier or kappa by themselves.
open_questions.first_step: Identify an immutable-source, unobserved-output caller and price all n+2^n-1 complete primitives, admission and dispatch.

coordination.overlap_scope: 100 live open PR titles, 60 recent account PRs, last 30 handoff comments, find_overlap helper over 340 open PRs and 2971 discussion records. Only PR4189 (n=1) and PR4225 (n=5) study unsigned F3 connectors. Closed work and arbitrary diffs are incompletely covered.
